title: JEPA World Models: From Prediction to Decisions
summary: An evidence-led tutorial that tests when predictive representations help action selection—and when accurate prediction is not enough.
description: This research tutorial connects JEPA representation learning, action-conditioned prediction, planning, uncertainty, and decision evaluation. It includes local LeJEPA-style objective studies, a verified inference check with an official V-JEPA 2.1 checkpoint, and clearly labeled MountainCar analogues. Notebook 23 v1 remains exploratory because all five JEPA fits triggered low spread. A separate v2 validation study found that rendered observations contain usable position and velocity information, but its supervised visual control and all nine JEPA fits failed preregistered state or action-fidelity gates. Independent test data, multi-step rollouts, and planning stayed closed. Toy results are not presented as paper reproductions. A genuine learned-JEPA-versus-direct-policy benchmark remains future work.

status.label: Active research tutorial
status.summary: Local lessons and evidence are available. Notebook 22 and Notebook 23 v1 are complete, with their stated limits. The v2 action-fidelity validation is a retained negative result: the visual positive control and all JEPA candidates failed their frozen gates, so held-out and planning stages stayed closed. A fresh preregistered positive-control study is required before a learned-JEPA-versus-direct-policy benchmark.

researchQuestion: When do predictive representations actually improve action selection, and when does accurate prediction fail to translate into effective decisions?

verifiedFindings.title: Small local objective studies produced mixed probe results
verifiedFindings.summary: On a five-seed CIFAR-10 subset, the SIGReg frozen-probe difference was -0.24 points (95% interval [-1.591, 1.111], including zero). In a separate five-seed study, RDMReg improved the local projector probe by 6.94 points over a weak teaching proxy, while the encoder-probe difference was 0.06 points.
verifiedFindings.scope: Two local CIFAR-10 subset studies with small CNNs; five seeds per study.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: Neither result is the corresponding ImageNet paper benchmark. The RDMReg result is sensitive to a degenerate teaching proxy.

verifiedFindings.title: Near-perfect action ranking did not make local MPC successful
verifiedFindings.summary: The state model ranked 60/60 non-tied action pairs correctly, yet MPC reached 0/20 goals and a direct momentum rule reached 20/20. The planner used 7.68 million model transitions and 12.747 seconds; the rule used no model transitions and 0.007 seconds.
verifiedFindings.scope: One deterministic polynomial Ridge model; MountainCarContinuous; 20 paired starts.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: Not a JEPA result or matched-actual-compute comparison. It applies only to the recorded local task and settings.

verifiedFindings.title: A hand-written controller prior changed CEM outcomes
verifiedFindings.summary: On 20 paired starts, neutral-start CEM reached 0/20 goals; momentum-prior CEM and direct control each reached 20/20. Direct control used zero model calls and averaged fewer steps than the prior planner.
verifiedFindings.scope: One fixed color-moment feature extractor and one Ridge fit on rendered MountainCar frames.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: The prior is hand-written, not a learned policy. This is not PiJEPA or a learned JEPA planner.

verifiedFindings.title: Planner-shift coverage intervals were wider across five fits
verifiedFindings.summary: For 90% prediction intervals, mean position coverage was 90.7% [89.7%, 91.7%] on random actions and 89.0% [82.2%, 95.7%] under planner shift.
verifiedFindings.scope: Five independent state-space Ridge ensembles on MountainCarContinuous.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: Not a JEPA uncertainty result; five fits and one task do not establish general calibration.

verifiedFindings.title: Visual JEPA outcomes depended on protocol and representation diagnostics
verifiedFindings.summary: Notebook 22 ranked 153/295 non-tied action pairs correctly; uniform-start JEPA CEM succeeded on 0/100 starts and momentum-prior CEM on 100/100, while direct control reached 20/20. In separate Notebook 23 v1, JEPA ranked 131/225 pairs correctly but succeeded on 0/100 starts with either initialization; all five JEPA fits triggered low spread. The direct controller reached 20/20, and the exact oracle reached 0/20 without the momentum prior and 20/20 with it.
verifiedFindings.scope: Two separate synthetic MountainCar studies. Notebook 22 used five learned model seeds; v1 used five paired model/data seeds and 20 shared evaluation starts.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: The studies use different objectives and protocols. All v1 JEPA fits triggered low spread, and v1 omitted prior-only CEM and a learned direct policy. These results do not establish a JEPA decision advantage or a general result, and are not paper reproductions.

verifiedFindings.title: Rendered state is recoverable, but the learned visual controls failed action-fidelity gates
verifiedFindings.summary: Across three paired seeds, a deterministic frame estimator had about 0.00375 position MAE and 0.000056 velocity MAE on train and validation data, and exact dynamics matched labels within 6e-8. The supervised visual model and all nine JEPA fits failed frozen validation gates. VISReg-style embeddings passed spread and rank checks, but velocity-probe R² stayed between 0.008 and 0.018.
verifiedFindings.scope: Synthetic MountainCar; three paired model/data seeds; three JEPA objective settings; 15 completed fits; 14.28 GPU-minutes on an RTX 5070.
verifiedFindings.claimBoundary: The result shows failure under this local frozen training recipe. It does not identify a general JEPA limitation or a causal loss defect. No independent test trajectories, multi-step rollouts, or planning outcomes were collected because the supervised visual control failed its gate. This is not a paper reproduction.

pendingWork.title: Matched learned-JEPA versus direct-policy benchmark
pendingWork.summary: First, preregister a fresh visual supervised positive-control study that targets small action effects and passes state and action-fidelity gates. Only then compare oracle dynamics, learned state-space dynamics, supervised visual dynamics, action-conditioned JEPA dynamics, a direct policy, prior-only planning, and policy-guided planning on shared held-out cases with compute accounting.
pendingWork.claimBoundary: The v2 visual positive control and all nine JEPA fits failed validation. Do not tune against those validation records or claim a JEPA planning result. Any follow-up requires a new protocol, fresh independent test cases, and a passing positive control before opening held-out evaluation.

pendingWork.title: Evaluate physical-state grounding in a released JEPA checkpoint
pendingWork.summary: Assess latent probes, planning, and policy outcomes for PSG-JEPA using a verified task setup and its released LIBERO-Goal checkpoint.
pendingWork.claimBoundary: The public release lists one training seed while the paper reports three-seed results. Check code, dataset, base-model, simulator, and checkpoint terms; a single checkpoint evaluation cannot reproduce the paper mean.

media.alt: Position and velocity coverage of nominal 90 percent prediction intervals on random-action and planner-shift tests. Means are near 90 percent; planner-shift confidence intervals are wider.
media.caption: Coverage means and 95% Student-t intervals across five independent state-space model fits.

media.alt: Four-panel dashboard for two separate synthetic MountainCar studies. It shows historical and v1 planner success, per-seed action ranking on a shared task-return score, JEPA spread and probe diagnostics, and success against transition calls and elapsed time. All five v1 JEPA fits triggered low spread.
media.caption: Notebook 22 and v1 are separate protocols. The v1 dashboard covers 660 episodes, 20 shared starts, five paired model/data seeds, and 960 interventions. JEPA outcomes are exploratory because all five v1 fits triggered low spread. Prior-only CEM was not run; oracle and learned methods used different devices.

media.alt: Architecture diagram of the local visual JEPA study, from generated frames through latent prediction and CEM planning, with direct-control and privileged-state baselines.
media.caption: The diagram describes the local synthetic study, not a published-paper implementation. The SVG has a title and description for assistive technology.

media.alt: Validation-only action-effect plots show raw predictions from each JEPA objective and visual control beside simulator changes for actions minus one, zero, and plus one. All seeds are shown. Several learned models predict effects that are much larger or point in the wrong direction.
media.caption: V2 uses 20 validation contexts per data seed. Dashed lines show simulator changes; colored lines show raw predictions before state clipping. The held-out test and planning stages stayed closed.

media.alt: Each point is one seed. SIGReg and variance-covariance models have low embedding spread. VISReg-style models pass spread and rank checks but all objectives have weak velocity probes.
media.caption: Representation diagnostics for nine JEPA fits and three supervised visual fits. Probe fits use training data and report validation scores.

media.alt: Seed-level comparison of effective rank, velocity-probe R-squared, and normalized action-contrast error. None of the JEPA objective settings passes all gates, and the supervised visual control fails its gate.
media.caption: Descriptive validation results across the frozen objective settings. The supervised visual control failed, so the objective comparison does not establish causal superiority.

media.alt: Architecture diagram: rendered frame pairs enter a visual encoder; an action-conditioned predictor outputs a predicted latent; a frozen state readout feeds the planner and environment feedback loop.
media.caption: Local synthetic MountainCar experiment path. The frozen state readout is a diagnostic linear probe, not a pixel decoder.
